texts.preamble: Vallem Kondu Ramanaiah Ramana, vs The State Of Andhra Pradesh on 17 September, 2019 Author: U. Durga Prasad Rao Bench: U. Durga Prasad Rao Hon'Ble Sri Justice U. Durga Prasad Rao Criminal Petition No.4969 Of 2019 Order:
texts.facts: The petitioner/accused seeks to quash the proceedings against him in Sessions Case No.111 of 2019 on the file of Additional Senior Civil Judge - cum - Additional Assistant Sessions Judge, Fast Track Court, Badvel, which was taken cognizance for the offences under Sections 188, 272, 273, 328 and Sections 57, 58 r/w 26, 30 of Food Safety and Standards Act (for short, 'FSS Act'). 2. The allegations against the petitioner briefly are that on 27.09.2018 at about 03.00 p.m., when the complainant along with his staff conducted raid in the petitioner's godown located at D.No.4-1-111, Anjaneya Nagar, Badvel Town, found the banned tobacco products and hence, seized the same and registered a case in Crime No.472 of 2018 of Badvel Urban Police Station, for the offences stated supra.
texts.arguments: 3. Learned counsel for petitioner while denying the FIR allegations would submit that even if the prosecution case is accepted to be true, tobacco products would not fall within the definition of Section 3(j) of FSS Act and therefore, the Police are not authorized to register the crime, investigate and file charge sheet and therefore, registration of the FIR is contrary to the provisions of FSS Act. He relied upon the order of this Court in Crl.P.Nos.3731 of 2018 and batch, dated 27.08.2018. So far as the offence under Section 188 of IPC is concerned, as per Section 195(1)(a)(i) of Cr.P.C, no Court shall take cognizance of the said offence except on the complaint in writing of that Court or by such Officer of the Court as that Court may authorise in writing in this behalf, or of some other Court to which that Court is subordinate.
texts.petitioner_arguments: 3. Learned counsel for petitioner while denying the FIR allegations would submit that even if the prosecution case is accepted to be true, tobacco products would not fall within the definition of Section 3(j) of FSS Act and therefore, the Police are not authorized to register the crime, investigate and file charge sheet and therefore, registration of the FIR is contrary to the provisions of FSS Act. He relied upon the order of this Court in Crl.P.Nos.3731 of 2018 and batch, dated 27.08.2018.
